metadata.title: Tomato & Ricotta Roulade - A delicious savoury vegetarian recipe
metadata.description:
This vibrant roulade recipe from Jenny Linford makes the perfect summer dish to serve for friends. A light and tasty mixture of ricotta cheese, cherry tomatoes and fresh herbs are wrapped up and baked in a simple tomato roulade - the result is a fantastic sharing dish, ready to slice up and serve with a green salad and cold glass of white wine. Delicious!

The recipe is taken from 'The Tomato Basket' by Jenny Linford, published by Ryland Peters & Small. Find more delicious tomato recipes in the book: http://rylandpeters.com/the-tomato-basket

Music from: audionautix.com
Editing by Louis Rizzo-Naudi: https://vimeo.com/louisrizzonaudi

A person is making a dish called tomato and ricotta rollade. They add various ingredients, mix them together, place them in a pan, and then bake it in the oven. Once cooked, they plate and serve it.
The video starts with a close-up of a cookbook cover, with the recipe title "Tomato and Ricotta Rollade" overlaid on it. summary.brief: A cook prepares a tomato‑and‑ricotta rollade, bakes it, and serves the sliced rolls with greens.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a close‑up of a cookbook cover titled “Tomato and Ricotta Rollade.” In the kitchen the cook melts butter with a bay leaf, adds flour to form a roux, then gradually whiskes in whole milk until a thick paste forms. Tomato puree is stirred in, followed by three egg yolks. Stiffly beaten egg whites are folded in to lighten the batter, which is spread onto a greased, parchment‑lined Swiss‑roll tin and baked until set. After cooling, a filling is made by halving cherry tomatoes, dicing the skins, and mixing them with chopped chives, parsley, lemon zest, black pepper, and ricotta cheese. The filling is spread over the cooled sheet, which is rolled up from the short side, placed on a baking tray, sprinkled with grated Parmesan, and baked again. The finished rollade is sliced, arranged on a plate with a bed of arugula, the plate is briefly flipped, and the video ends with promotional title cards.

summary.brief: A woman prepares a tomato‑ricotta roulade, baking the batter, adding a fresh filling, rolling it, and serving sliced pieces.
summary.detailed: The cook melts butter in a saucepan, adds a bay leaf and flour, and cooks the mixture for about a minute to form a thick paste. She gradually pours in whole milk while stirring until the béchamel thickens, then discards the bay leaf, seasons with salt and pepper, and stirs in tomato puree. Three egg yolks are beaten into the mixture. Separately, she whips egg whites to stiff peaks, folds a spoonful into the batter to loosen it, then gently folds in the remaining whites, creating a light batter. The batter is spread evenly onto a greased Swiss‑roll pan and baked at 200 °C for 12‑15 minutes. After removing it from the oven, she covers the sheet with a clean kitchen cloth to cool. While it cools, she halves cherry tomatoes, removes the cores, dices the skins, and chops fresh chives and parsley. She adds lemon zest, a pinch of black pepper, and ricotta cheese, mixing everything into a filling. The filling is spread uniformly over the cooled batter sheet, which is then rolled tightly from the short side, placed on a baking tray, sprinkled with grated Parmesan, and baked again for about 20 minutes. The warm roulade is finally sliced and arranged on a plate beside a green salad.

summary_sent_to_llm.description:
This vibrant roulade recipe from Jenny Linford makes the perfect summer dish to serve for friends. A light and tasty mixture of ricotta cheese, cherry tomatoes and fresh herbs are wrapped up and baked in a simple tomato roulade - the result is a fantastic sharing dish, ready to slice up and serve with a green salad and cold glass of white wine. Delicious!

The recipe is taken from 'The Tomato Basket' by Jenny Linford, published by Ryland Peters & Small. Find more delicious tomato recipes in the book: http://rylandpeters.com/the-tomato-basket

Music from: audionautix.com
Editing by Louis Rizzo-
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with a close‑up of a cookbook cover titled “Tomato and Ricotta Rollade.” In the kitchen the cook melts butter with a bay leaf, adds flour to form a roux, then gradually whiskes in whole milk until a thick paste forms. Tomato puree is stirred in, followed by three egg yolks. Stiffly beaten egg whites are folded in to lighten the batter, which is spread onto a greased, parchment‑lined Swiss‑roll tin and baked until set. After cooling, a filling is made by halving cherry tomatoes, dicing the skins, and mixing them with chopped chives, parsley, lemon zest, black pepper, and ricotta cheese. The filling is spread over the cooled sheet, which is rolled up from the short side, placed on a baking tray, sprinkled with grated Parmesan, and baked again. The finished rollade is sliced, arranged on a plate with a bed of arugula, the plate is briefly flipped, and the video ends with promotional title cards.
